history.summary: Hindu temple dedicated to Ahalya at the legendary site of Maharishi Gautama's ashram, where Rama freed Ahalya from her stone curse (Ramayana). The sanctum's main object of worship is a flat stone said to bear Sita's footprints; the shrine also holds statues of Ahalya, Rama, Lakshmana, Gautama and Vishvamitra. The present structure was built 1662-1682 under Maharaja Chhatra Singh and Maharaja Rudra Singh of the Darbhanga Raj and is described as the first Ram-Janaki temple in India. CSV TOWN CORRECTION: not in Darbhanga city - it stands in Ward 11 of Kamtaul (Ahiyari South), about 24 km northwest of Darbhanga. Opening-hours conflict: listings say 5:00 AM-9:00 PM daily vs 5:00 AM-10:00 PM - verify locally. Coordinates from geocoder POI 'Ahilya Asthan, Ahiari, Jale', corroborated by an independent location listing.

name: Ahalya Sthan Mandir (Gautam Ashram)
town_description: Kamtaul is a small city in Darbhanga district, Bihar, about 24 km northwest of Darbhanga town, with its own railway station (about 4 km from the temple). The Ahalya Sthan temple stands in its Ahiyari South locality (Ward 11).

travel.railway: Kamtaul Railway Station (about 4 km); Darbhanga Junction (about 24 km)
travel.road: By road via Kamtaul, about 24 km northwest of Darbhanga on SH-75 (verify route)

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Ramnavami fair in Chaitra (March-April) is the main festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM-9:00 PM daily per most listings; one listing says 10:00 PM close - verify locally
